housing: Teignbridge runs from the coast at Dawlish and Teignmouth to the edge of Dartmoor, with Newton Abbot as the main town. Private renting is a little below the national average, with lets in the Victorian terraces and flats of Newton Abbot and the seaside towns. Inland towns and villages have stone, cob and thatched cottages, many listed and some off the gas grid. Holiday and second homes are common on the coast.
checkinTips: Seaside homes in Dawlish and Teignmouth: check window frames, metal fittings and outside paintwork for salt and wind damage.
Cob and thatched cottages in the villages: photograph the thatch, walls, low beams and any damp or cracks in limewashed walls.
Dartmoor-edge homes in Bovey Tracey and Ashburton: record oil tanks or LPG, wood burners and the sweep certificate.
Victorian flat conversions in Teignmouth and Newton Abbot: note shared hallways, fire doors and keys for each door.
Homes near the Teign estuary and rivers: check ground floors and walls for damp or past flood marks.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can contact Teignbridge District Council's Private Sector Housing team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions.
